findings.title: Vital reschedule drops calendar and video cleanup
findings.body: Reschedule now awaits the async getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). Array.forEach never waits for async callbacks and discards their return values, so the try/catch around the loop cannot see failures. getCalendar suspends on a dynamic app import before calendar.deleteEvent is called, and the video branch only returns deleteMeeting, which itself now awaits getVideoAdapters before calling the provider. Nothing awaits those floating promises. The function then sends the reschedule email and returns true. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least issued before the function continued. After this change a serverless worker can finish the request and freeze before the import resumes, so the cancelled booking's calendar event and video meeting are never removed (the slot stays busy and attendees still see the old event). Rejections become unhandled promise rejections. Await the references with for...of or Promise.all, including both deleteEvent and deleteMeeting, before sending email.

findings.title: WipeMyCal reschedule drops calendar and video cleanup
findings.body: The WipeMyCal reschedule handler awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not await async callbacks and ignores what they return, so the surrounding try/catch never handles rejections. Because app modules are now dynamic imports, getCalendar yields before calendar.deleteEvent runs, and the video branch returns deleteMeeting without awaiting it even though deleteMeeting now waits on getVideoAdapters before deleting the meeting. The handler proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns true while that work is still suspended. Before this change getCalendar was sync, so the calendar delete was started before the function moved on. On serverless the process can exit when the handler returns, leaving the old calendar event and video room in place after the booking is marked cancelled. Use for...of or Promise.all and await both provider deletes before sending email.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not wait for provider cancellation
findings.body: requestReschedule awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not join those promises, so the mutation continues, sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, and resolves while calendar deletion is still suspended on the app-store dynamic import. The video branch only returns deleteMeeting from that callback; deleteMeeting now awaits getVideoAdapters before it calls the provider, so that cleanup is deferred the same way and is also not awaited. The booking row is already set to CANCELLED before this loop. If the worker stops when the tRPC mutation returns, which is typical on serverless, the provider calls never run and the old calendar event and video room remain. There is no try/catch around the loop, so a rejection is unhandled rather than a failed mutation. Await the references with for...of or Promise.all, including deleteEvent and deleteMeeting, before email or webhooks.

findings.title: Recurring cancel never joins calendar deletions
findings.body: Cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking deletes external calendar events with credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }). forEach does not return those promises, and the push onto apiDeletes happens only after deleteEvent has already resolved, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) neither starts nor waits for this work. This change made getCalendar async (it now awaits a dynamic import) while leaving this loop in place; the non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten as a for...of that awaits getCalendar and pushes the in-flight deleteEvent promise. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was invoked before the callback's first await and the provider request was at least started. Now the callback suspends before deleteEvent is issued. The handler can mark the series CANCELLED, send the cancellation email, and return while those events are still on the external calendar; on serverless the continuations are often dropped. Failures are unhandled rejections. Replace the forEach with a for...of or Promise.all and include each deleteEvent promise in apiDeletes before awaiting them.
